sections.h2: Selling a Carrollton house: your routes
sections.html:
Carrollton owners have three choices: engage an agent, go it alone, or turn the keys over to a cash buyer who accepts the property untouched. Condition, timing and any tenant or co-owner complications steer the choice.

  • Agent listing: the biggest buyer pool, along with showings, inspection requests and lender deadlines.
  • Private sale: no listing agent, though pricing and paperwork land on you.
  • Cash purchase: fewer steps and no repair demands, at a price usually below a polished listing.

Renters outnumber owners in Carrollton. Homeownership stands at 41.0 percent for 2020 to 2024, and just 73.9 percent of people lived at the same address twelve months earlier, which signals frequent moves. Expect landlords and investors among your buyers.

sections.h2: The University of West Georgia and your street
sections.html:
The University of West Georgia occupies the western side of Carrollton, and its story starts in the city. In 1907, trustees bought the 275-acre Bluford Sharp farm west of town for $9,625 as the Fourth District A&M School site, and classes began in January 1908. The Board of Regents picked the Carrollton campus on April 15, 1933, and it became West Georgia College, then the State University of West Georgia in 1996 and the University of West Georgia on January 12, 2005.

Campus influence fades with distance. Before assuming student demand reaches your block, ask a local agent or investor how far your house sits from it.

Carrollton had an estimated 27,925 residents in mid-2025, up 4.5 percent from its 2020 base, across 22.41 square miles of land. The measures below cover 2020 to 2024.

House values sit a little under the national midpoint, while incomes and rents sit well under it. Owners with a mortgage pay a midpoint $1,590 a month, against $1,963 nationally. Owners with no mortgage carry a midpoint $632 a month, close to the $638 national figure. With incomes lower than average, affordability limits many local buyers, and a house needing work may lose more value in a retail sale than the repair would cost. Households number 9,992 and average 2.45 people.

Carrollton City Schools runs its own district with four schools on a single 130-acre campus: Carrollton Elementary, Carrollton Upper Elementary, Carrollton Middle School and Carrollton High. Whether an address lies inside that district depends on the city limits, so confirm it with the school system before putting it in a listing. Parents ask about schools first, and a correct answer helps a serious buyer move faster. Some families treat having all four schools on one campus as a selling point, so mention it if your house is close by.

sections.h2: Selling a rented or worn Carrollton house
sections.html:
Because so many Carrollton homes are rentals, a lot of sales involve a tenant. A house can sell with the lease still running or after it ends. Give each buyer the lease, the rent ledger and the deposit amount at the start, so no one is surprised later. A cash buyer who accepts the house as-is can take it subject to the lease, which spares you from clearing the unit and staging it for showings.

If the house needs work, weigh the two paths side by side. A retail buyer with a loan brings an appraisal and an inspection, and repair requests often follow. A cash buyer prices the repairs in and closes on a date you choose. Ask for each offer in writing and compare what you would take home after commission, carrying costs and repairs, not just the top-line number.

Carrollton added a short-term rental article to its code in July 2025, as Chapter 18, Article VI. A short-term rental is a dwelling, or part of one, rented for lodging for 30 consecutive days or fewer, and no one may rent without a license.

  • The license is annual, with a non-refundable $500 application fee filed with Community Development.
  • Occupancy tops out at two adults per bedroom, with one vehicle per bedroom parked on paved surfaces, never on the street.
  • External signs are banned, and the license number must appear on every online listing.
  • Three convictions or judgments for code violations trigger a 12-month revocation.
  • Appeals of a denial, suspension or revocation go in writing to the Mayor and City Council within 30 calendar days.

Hotel-motel tax applies as well. Each license is tied to one owner and one address, so a buyer planning a rental must obtain a new one. The city's licensing and permit office, which also handles code enforcement, occupational tax and alcohol licensing, answers questions at 770-830-2000. Rentals also remain subject to occupational tax, regulatory fees, business licenses and the zoning ordinance, so check where your parcel is zoned before you pitch it to investors.

The county, not the city, appraises and bills Carrollton property. Each parcel's fair market value is fixed on January 1, assessment is 40 percent of that, and a mill is one dollar per thousand dollars of assessed value. Rates come from several bodies: commissioners for county operations, the school board for schools, and the state, capped at a quarter mill.

An appeal begins at the county assessors' board and may continue to the Board of Equalization, a panel the grand jury appoints. You can choose arbitration instead. Georgia notices carry a 45-day appeal window, so rely on the date printed on yours. The Board of Assessors takes returns and homestead applications, while the tax commissioner prepares and collects bills. Call 770-830-5843 about calculations, late payments and interest, or 770-830-5826 for the tag and tax office.

sections.h2: Papers to gather and the transfer tax
sections.html:
Before you accept an offer, collect what a buyer will request: the latest assessment notice, any lease and rent ledger, a copy of a short-term rental license if one exists, and permits for past work. Georgia's transfer tax also applies to the sale. It is a dollar on the first thousand of price plus a dime for each further hundred or fraction, and the seller bears it unless the contract provides otherwise. For exemption questions, contact the Carroll County superior court clerk.

A cash buyer skips the appraisal and the lender's checklist, so the closing date is whatever you both agree to. Ask your closing professional how rent, deposits and the year's tax will be prorated on the settlement statement.

faqs.q: Do most Carrollton households own their homes?
faqs.a: No. Homeownership is 41.0 percent for 2020 to 2024, against 65.2 percent nationally, so most households rent.
About 27,900: 27,925 in the mid-2025 estimate, up from 26,738 in the 2020 census and 24,388 in 2010.

faqs.q: Do Airbnb-style rentals need a license in Carrollton?
faqs.a: Yes. For stays of 30 consecutive days or fewer, the city requires an annual license with a $500 non-refundable application fee, and the license cannot pass to a new owner.

faqs.q: Which office bills property tax on a Carrollton house?
faqs.a: Carroll County. Its assessors set the values, and the county tax commissioner prepares bills, collects payment and answers questions at 770-830-5843.

faqs.q: Is a tenant-occupied Carrollton house sellable?
faqs.a: Yes. A buyer who pays cash and accepts the house as-is can take it subject to the lease. Share the lease terms early, and find out from your closing professional how deposits and prepaid rent are handled.
